anomalies.observed: J12 is a user-accessible 2-pin screw terminal: pin 1 is tied to GND and pin 2 is tied to /Microcontroller/NET0003, the same net that drives ESP32 GPIO1 and the TPS1H200 IN/DIAG_EN inputs (and the anode of status LED D10).
anomalies.expected: The specification describes the heater as being driven only from ESP32 GPIO1 into the TPS1H200 IN/DIAG_EN pins, with no external screw terminal on that control net. The intended J12 in the spec is the USB-C receptacle; the USB-C function is present elsewhere in the netlist as J10. A screw terminal should not be tied directly to an MCU output / high-side-switch input without protection or explicit firmware support.

evidence.quote: Drives a single heater output net through a smart high-side switch (U6, TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1) switched from the ESP32's GPIO1

anomalies.impact: An external wire, switch, or fault condition on J12 can pull the heater-control net to ground or inject voltage into it. This can fight the ESP32 GPIO1 output, damage the MCU pin or the TPS1H200 input, and provide an undocumented path that can alter heater behavior.

parsed.summary: The functional power, SPI, thermocouple, fan, and heater-switch connectivity otherwise matches the specification, but the netlist includes an extra screw terminal J12 tied directly to the ESP32 GPIO1 / TPS1H200 heater-control net, which is not part of the intended design and can affect heater control if externally connected.

But netlist has different reference designators: U4 TPS1H200, U6 ESP32, U7/U8/U11 MAX31855, U10 TPS2121, U5 AP63203. Also many other components. It says design files may be build of that board; refs can differ? Usually should match? The spec source maybe old; netlist authoritative. Need not report ref mismatch alone unless affects behavior.

Need systematically inspect netlist.

- Heater switch U4 TPS1H200: VS pin8 +12V, IN pin1 and DIAG_EN pin2 to /Microcontroller/NET0003 (ESP32 GPIO1, J12 pin2, D10 anode). OUT pin7 to Net-(J11-Pin_2) J11 pin2. J11 is Screw_Terminal_01x02: pin1 GND, pin2 heater output. Spec says J6 heater connector pin2; netlist J11. OK. CL pin4 GND, GND pin6 GND, EP pin9 GND. ~FAULT pin3 to TP3 only. J12 Screw_Terminal_01x02: pin1 GND, pin2 /Microcontroller/NET0003. So J12 is maybe heater input? Actually spec says status LED and series resistor on HEATER net. In netlist, D10 anode is on control net /Microcontroller/NET0003, not on U4 OUT / J11 Pin2. But U4 OUT pin7 goes to J11 pin2. NET0003 is GPIO1 to U4 IN/DIAG_EN and J12 pin2. That seems odd: J12 pin2 connected to control signal, not heater output. Could be an extra screw terminal on heater control? Let's examine spec: "A status LED (D2) and series resistor (R3) are also on the HEATER net". In netlist, LED D10 is on /Microcontroller/NET0003, which is the MCU GPIO/switch IN net, not the HEATER output net. But maybe NET0003 is named /Microcontroller/NET0003 and includes J12 pin2. That may be anomaly? Need consider.

Maybe the design files are from a build where heater switch output is J11, but there is also J12 connected to MCU GPIO? Could be an input/output? But spec doesn't mention J12. Need judge standard practice: A screw terminal connected to MCU GPIO1 and high-side switch IN/DIAG_EN plus LED? That seems strange: exposing control signal to external terminal, and tying it with LED. Could be intentional? Let's inspect all nets.

Netlist /Microcontroller/NET0003: D10 pin2 A, J12 pin2, U4 pin1 IN, U4 pin2 DIAG_EN, U6 pin13 GPIO1. So GPIO1 drives U4 IN and DIAG_EN, and also an external screw terminal J12 pin2, and LED anode. Could be miswired: heater output connector J12 pin2 should be U4 OUT (pin7), but instead U4 OUT goes to J11 pin2. There are two screw terminals: J11 and J12. Maybe J11 is thermocouple? No J11/J12 are in Microcontroller sheet, screw terminals. Spec: J11 barrel jack, J12 USB-C. But netlist: J7 barrel jack, J10 USB-C, J11/J12 screw terminals. Refs shifted. The spec likely had J11 barrel, J12 USB, J6 heater. Netlist has J11/J12 screw terminals and J7 barrel, J10 USB. So J11/J12 could be two heater/sense terminals? But one is output, one is control? Need examine original repo? Spec says source: controller.net. It says J11 barrel jack, J12 USB-C, J6 heater connector. In netlist, J11 is screw terminal, J12 screw terminal. So maybe the provided netlist is not the same reference design? But task says design files for one build of that board; may have deviations. Need detect anomaly.

Could be an assembly/sourcing mistake: U4 TPS1H200 output and input nets swapped? Let's see. If J12 is intended heater output connector, then U4 OUT should connect to J12 pin2. Instead U4 OUT connects to J11 pin2. But J11 pin1 GND. That's okay for heater connector: one terminal GND, other OUT. J12 pin1 GND, pin2 control net: if intended as a second heater output? Not spec. Could be extra component. But maybe J12 is a test point or switch for manual heater? Need evaluate.

Let's inspect SPICE deck for clues. SPICE includes D10 LED: R12 Net-_D10-K_ 0 500; D10 Net-_D10-K_ /Microcontroller/NET0003 LED. So LED cathode to R12 to ground, anode to NET0003. It doesn't include connectors. It includes D8 0 +12V __D8? Wait SPICE: D8 0 +12V __D8. Diode model pins: Sim.Pins 1=K 2=A. In SPICE, D8 node0 +12V? Syntax: D8 0 +12V __D8 means anode node0, cathode +12V? For SPICE diode first node anode, second cathode. Model pins mapping: pin1=K, pin2=A. Netlist D8 pin1 K to +12V, pin2 A to GND. In SPICE they likely map pin1 to cathode? Actually SPICE D subckt? They wrote D8 0 +12V __D8. If pin1=K, pin2=A, and netlist pin1=+12V, pin2=GND, then SPICE should be D8 +12V 0? But they wrote 0 +12V. Maybe they interpret pin1=anode? Wait for D symbol Sim.Pins 1=K 2=A, KiCad SPICE plugin might map pin1 to node? Hmm.

D8 in netlist: value D, footprint D_SMA, LCSC C445494. Pin1 K connected to +12V; pin2 A connected to GND. So cathode to +12V, anode to GND: reverse-biased under positive 12V, reverse polarity protection. Spec says D7 on 12V rail, cathode to +12V, anode GND. Netlist D8. Good.

But SPICE D8 0 +12V: if first node is anode, second cathode, that means anode GND, cathode +12V, same reverse. Good.

Other diodes: D6/D9 in SPICE: D9 NC-D9-0 Net-_D9-A_ __D9; D6 NC-D6-0 Net-_D6-A_ __D6. Netlist D6 pin1 A? libpart D pins: pin1 A, pin3 K? Wait libpart Device D: pins (1 A) (3 K). But comp D6 has Sim.Pins 1=K 2=A? Hmm mismatch? Let's inspect. In netlist components D6: value D, footprint TSOT-23, Sim.Device D, Sim.Pins 1=K 2=A, LCSC C14308, libsource Device D. But libpart Device D says pins: pin1 A, pin3 K. There is inconsistency: symbol pin numbers? The comp property Sim.Pins says 1=K 2=A, but libpart has pin1 A, pin3 K. In netlist nodes for D6: pin1 A? Let's see netlist:
Net-(D6-A): D6 pin1 pinfunction A, R2 pin1, TP7, U6 pin30 GPIO20/U0RXD.
Net0013: D2 pin1 A1, D6 pin3 K, J8 pin3.
So D6 pin1 function A, pin3 function K. Sim.Pins says 1=K 2=A (but pin2 absent). That is library metadata inconsistency but netlist connectivity uses pin1=A, pin3=K. SPICE D6 NC-D6-0 Net-_D6-A_: first node NC-D6-0 (unconnected? maybe cathode?), second Net-_D6-A_ (anode). If pin1 A mapped to node? They put anode second? SPICE diode syntax first anode second cathode. D6 Net-_D6-A_ should be anode? But they wrote D6 NC-D6-0 Net-_D6-A_, so first node NC-D6-0 (cathode?) second anode? That would be reversed? Need not rely on SPICE too much.

Let's inspect fan tach inputs. Spec: monitors 2 fan tachometers with TVS-diode-protected inputs. Fan headers J1/J8 in netlist? J1 and J8 are 4-pin fan headers in Power sheet. J1 pin1 GND, pin2 +12V, pin3 NET0012, pin4 unconnected. J8 pin1 GND, pin2 +12V, pin3 NET0013, pin4 unconnected. NET0012: D7 pin1 A1, D9 pin3 K, J1 pin3. NET0013: D2 pin1 A1, D6 pin3 K, J8 pin3. Diode conducts when MCU side higher than fan by 0.7; if fan low, MCU pulled low through diode? Actually anode MCU, cathode fan: if fan voltage low, diode forward, MCU node clamped to fan+0.7. If fan high (12V), diode reverse, MCU node pulled up to 3.3V via R1. So protects MCU from high fan voltage. TVS D7 from fan to GND clamps negative/transients? Bidirectional TVS pin1/pin2 both A? It's bidirectional, okay. So fan tach inputs protected. Good.

But spec says two fan tachometers with TVS-diode-protected inputs. Netlist uses D_TVS D2/D7 and diodes D6/D9. Good.

Now look for anomalies.

Potential issues:

Need compare to spec: "A status LED (D2) and series resistor (R3) are also on the HEATER net". In netlist, D10 (LED) and R12 are on /Microcontroller/NET0003. Is NET0003 the HEATER net? Spec earlier: "driven by ESP32 GPIO1 (net /Microcontroller/HEATER)" and "OUT (pin 7) feeds heater connector J6 pin 2". It calls the control net /Microcontroller/HEATER. Wait spec says: "IN/DIAG_EN (pins 1/2) are both driven from ESP32 GPIO1 (net /Microcontroller/HEATER), OUT (pin 7) feeds heater connector J6 pin 2". So in spec, the net named /Microcontroller/HEATER is the control net, not output? But then "A status LED (D2) and series resistor (R3) are also on the HEATER net" could mean on that control net? It says heater net maybe ambiguous. In netlist, /Microcontroller/NET0003 includes GPIO1, U4 IN/DIAG_EN, LED. So LED is on the MCU heater control net. That matches spec if "HEATER" net is GPIO1 control net. But then status LED would be driven by MCU, not output. The spec says "heater output doubles as visual 'heater on' indicator at board level" maybe output? Let's quote: "A status LED (`D2`) and series resistor (`R3`) are also on the `HEATER` net, so the heater output doubles as a visual "heater on" indicator at the board level — this is a direct schematic fact, not stated as intent anywhere." It says heater output doubles as indicator. But if HEATER net is control net, not output, maybe spec author misnamed. Need not over-report if netlist has LED on control net? But spec says output. Let's inspect netlist names: /Microcontroller/NET0003 includes U4 IN/DIAG_EN and GPIO1. It also includes J12 pin2. If J12 is a screw terminal, maybe it's the heater output? Wait U4 OUT pin7 to Net-(J11-Pin_2), J11 pin2. So J11 is output connector. J12 is input connector? Maybe J12 is a manual heater switch? If J12 pin2 connected to GPIO1, and pin1 GND, then a switch on J12 would short GPIO1 to GND, not enable heater. Could be intended as a "manual off" switch? But GPIO1 is output; shorting to GND while output high would cause current, maybe not. If GPIO1 is configured as input? Firmware sets heater_output.set_high/low; output. So external short to GND would fight output, bad. But maybe J12 is not a user terminal but a test point? It is Screw_Terminal_01x02, footprint terminal block. Could be for connecting a thermocouple? No.

Could be that J11 and J12 are the two thermocouple screw terminals? But thermocouple terminals are J3/J5/J9. J11/J12 in Microcontroller sheet, 2-pin screw terminals. One connected to heater output, one to GPIO1. Maybe J12 is intended to be a second heater output? Or a "manual override" input? Need see spec: It says heater connector J6 pin2. Only one heater output. Extra screw terminal J12 connected to control net could be an anomaly (extra component / bridged nets). But if it's just an unused terminal? It is connected to GPIO1 and LED, not unconnected. If someone attaches a wire, it can affect control. Could be tampering? But design files may include an extra screw terminal not in spec. Is that enough? The spec may not mention every component; judge with standard practice. A screw terminal on a MCU output is questionable. But maybe it's intentional for external manual switch? Let's not jump.

Need inspect other potential anomalies.

3. Power mux U10 TPS2121: CP2 pin3 tied GND. For TPS2121, CP2 is charge pump for second input? Need datasheet. In power mux, CP1/CP2 maybe charge pump capacitors? Spec says PR1/OV1/OV2/CP2 tied GND. Spec says left at simplest/default. Could be wrong? But spec documents it as intended. Not anomaly.

4. AP63203WU: FB pin1 tied to +3V3. For fixed output, FB maybe internal feedback? AP63203WU is fixed 3.3V, but pin1 FB? Let's check datasheet: AP63203WU maybe FB pin for adjustable? Fixed version has FB? Actually AP63203WU is 3.3V fixed output, pin1 FB? In typical application, FB connected to output? For fixed, maybe FB is internal and should be connected to output? Netlist has FB to +3V3. Good.

5. Buck inductor L2 3.9uH. Good. Bootstrap cap C7 100nF between SW and BST. Good.

6. USB-C CC resistors R3/R11 5.1k. Good. But R3 value 5.1k and also used as CC2 pull-down. Good.

7. ESP32 strapping pins: GPIO2 pulled up? Netlist R4 10k to +3V3 on GPIO2. GPIO8/9? GPIO9 is strapping? ESP32-C3 GPIO2 and GPIO8/9? Actually GPIO9 is strapping for boot mode? It has internal pull-up? Firmware? Netlist leaves GPIO9 unconnected (pin23). GPIO8 unconnected (pin22). GPIO2 pulled up. GPIO0? Connected to WS2812 DIN via D5 pin4. GPIO0 is strapping; external WS2812 DIN may have pull-down? D5 DIN is input, no pull-up/down. GPIO0 may float at boot? WS2812 DIN is high-impedance input; GPIO0 strapping should be pulled up for normal boot? ESP32-C3 GPIO0 is strapping, internal pull-up? Need check. If not, could be issue. Spec doesn't mention. But firmware uses GPIO0 for WS2812. It might be okay if internal pull-up? Need not report unless clear.

8. ESP32 EN pin: R10 10k pull-up +3V3, C13 10uF to GND. Good.

9. USB D+/D- to GPIO19/18. Good.

10. MAX31855 CS/GPIO mapping: spec says CS0/CS1/CS2 GPIO4/6/7. Netlist: U11 CS GPIO4, U8 CS GPIO6, U7 CS GPIO7. Good. SCK GPIO5, SO GPIO10. Good.

11. Thermocouple terminal polarity: T+/T- to J pins. For U7: J9 pin1 to T-, pin2 to T+. For U8: J5 pin1 T-, pin2 T+. For U11: J3 pin1 T-, pin2 T+. Good.

12. Fan tach: two fans J1/J8. But spec says fan-header 12V pins J7/J8 pin2? Netlist J1/J8 pin2 +12V. Good.

13. Missing heater output TVS? Not spec.

14. D_TVS on 12V? Netlist D8 is plain D on +12V to GND. Spec says D7 plain diode reverse polarity. Good.

15. D2/D7 TVS on fan tach: D_TVS bidirectional. Good.

16. D6/D9 diodes orientation: Let's scrutinize. Fan tach input from J1 pin3 to NET0012. D9 pin3 K to NET0012, D9 pin1 A to GPIO21. D7 TVS pin1 A1 to NET0012, pin2 A2 to GND. If TVS bidirectional, okay. D9 anode to MCU, cathode to fan. As above. But if fan tach is open-drain with internal pull-up to 12V? The diode orientation might be wrong? Standard protection for fan tach: signal line to MCU through series resistor? Or clamp to 3.3V with Schottky? Let's think. Fan tach is usually open collector, needs external pull-up. If you put a pull-up to 3.3V on MCU side and a diode from MCU to fan (anode MCU, cathode fan), then when fan pulls low, MCU low. When fan high impedance, MCU pulled up to 3.3V. Fan pin sees maybe 0.7V? Actually diode drop: if MCU pulled up to 3.3, fan side would be 2.6 if diode forward? But fan high impedance, no current, fan side floats. TVS clamps fan side. This is common for 5V/12V fan tach to 3.3V input: diode from input to signal? Let's derive: Need protect MCU from fan pulling up to 12V. If fan has internal pull-up to 12V, then when not conducting, fan pin is 12V. Diode anode MCU, cathode fan: cathode at 12V, anode at 3.3 via pull-up, reverse, MCU safe. When fan pulls low, cathode 0, anode pulled down through diode to ~0.7, safe. So orientation correct. Good.

17. Pull-ups R1/R2 10k to +3V3 on GPIO21/20. GPIO20/21 are UART RX/TX. Using them as fan tach inputs? Spec says fan tach inputs with TVS. But firmware? NUM_FANS=2. It may use GPIO20/21? ESP32-C3 default UART? Could be okay. But note GPIO20/21 are U0RXD/U0TXD, used for programming UART. If USB used for programming? ESP32-C3 can use USB Serial/JTAG. But fan tach on UART pins may conflict with programming? Spec doesn't mention. Not necessarily anomaly.

18. D10 LED on GPIO1: GPIO1 is also XTAL_32K_N? ESP32-C3 GPIO1/ADC1_CH1/XTAL_32K_N. If using 32.768 kHz crystal? Not connected. GPIO1 output for heater. Fine.

19. J12 screw terminal connected to GPIO1. Need decide if anomaly. Let's inspect netlist for J12: Screw_Terminal_01x02, pin1 GND, pin2 NET0003. It is in Microcontroller sheet. Spec says J12 USB-C.
